Vision

The Swartz Center for Computational Neuroscience should become the world’s leading open EEG methods and infrastructure center: a place where electrophysiological theory, scalable computation, and interoperable data systems are developed as one scientific instrument.

SCCN is uniquely positioned for this role. EEGLAB remains a central open environment for EEG, MEG, and related electrophysiological analysis, with ICA, time frequency analysis, artifact modeling, visualization, scripting, and an extensible plugin ecosystem. NEMAR extends that tradition from software to data infrastructure by connecting BIDS formatted EEG, MEG, and iEEG datasets with OpenNeuro, quality visualization, and high performance computing through SDSC and NSG. Together, EEGLAB and NEMAR can define a full stack for EEG science: acquisition aware metadata, interoperable formats, reproducible preprocessing, large scale analysis, model training, benchmarking, and open dissemination.

The next phase should center on big data EEG and neuro AI. SCCN should build shared pipelines that make public and local EEG datasets machine readable, analysis ready, and model ready, using BIDS, HED, EEGLAB, Python, TensorFlow, PyTorch, and cloud or supercomputing back ends. Deep learning should not replace biophysically informed EEG methods, but should be integrated with them: source modeling, ICA, event annotation, quality control, representation learning, foundation models, and cross dataset generalization should become mutually reinforcing parts of one framework. Recent NEMAR expansion toward petabyte scale, in place computing and multimodal neuro AI makes this a natural trajectory.

The vision is for SCCN to make EEG a mature data intensive science: interoperable by default, reproducible by design, scalable from single participants to global archives, and interpretable enough to link neural dynamics to behavior, cognition, clinical state, and human experience.

Arnaud Delorme, co-director
Tzyy Ping Jung, director
